panels.visual: The Acropolis in April 1941 with a huge dark-red occupation banner (no symbols) hanging from the flagpole above the temples, grey-uniformed soldiers small in the distance, a sad dark sky, Glauka in the corner
panels.caption: In April 1941 the German army took Athens. They raised their banner on the Acropolis.

panels.visual: Two Greek students (young men in dark jackets) creeping up the rock at night under the moon, tiptoeing
panels.caption: On the night of 30 May 1941 two students climbed up.

panels.visual: The two students tearing the banner down from its pole at night, flag falling like a cloth, hearts racing
panels.caption: Manolis Glezos and Apostolos Santas tore the flag down and took it away.

panels.visual: A young Greek guard wrapped in the Greek flag on the rock edge in a hazy memory-like dotted frame with a question mark
panels.caption: A story says a young guard, Konstantinos Koukidis, wrapped himself in the flag and jumped. Historians are not sure it happened.
